before.stem: Regarding the olfactory nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT: (x) The olfactory bulb lies in the posterior cranial fossa. 10% The olfactory nerve is the longest cranial nerve. 7%
options: The olfactory nerve originates from the medulla oblongata.
The olfactory nerve carries crude touch sensation from the nasal cavity.
The olfactory tract runs inferiorly to the frontal lobe.
before.explanation: The olfactory nerve is the shortest cranial nerve and originates from the cerebrum; it is one of two nerves that do not originate from the brainstem, the other being the optic nerve. Olfactory nerve fibres enter the skull via the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone to enter to olfactory bulb in the anterior cranial fossa before passing into the olfactory tract which lies inferior to the frontal lobe. } Vv

after.stem: Regarding the olfactory nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The olfactory bulb lies in the posterior cranial fossa.
The olfactory nerve is the longest cranial nerve.
The olfactory nerve originates from the medulla oblongata.
The olfactory nerve carries crude touch sensation from the nasal cavity.
The olfactory tract runs inferiorly to the frontal lobe.
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: The olfactory tract lies inferior to the frontal lobe; CN I enters through the cribriform plate and the bulb lies in the anterior cranial fossa.
after.learningNote: The olfactory tract lies inferior to the frontal lobe; CN I enters through the cribriform plate and the bulb lies in the anterior cranial fossa.
after.highYieldNote: The olfactory tract lies inferior to the frontal lobe; CN I enters through the cribriform plate and the bulb lies in the anterior cranial fossa.
after.mnemonic: I smells under the frontal lobe.
